prompt: Ontario licenses new drivers in three steps.
explanation: True. This system is called graduated licensing.

prompt: How many steps does graduated licensing have?
explanation: Graduated licensing has three steps: Class G1, Class G2, then full Class G. The rules ease at each step.

prompt: The steps are G1, G2 and full ___.
explanation: The last step is full Class G.

prompt: Which is the first step?
explanation: Class G1 is the first step.

prompt: Graduated licensing puts G2 before G1.
explanation: False. G1 is the first step, then G2.

prompt: Which step gives full car privileges?
explanation: Class G is the full licence for cars, vans and small trucks.

prompt: Class G is the full licence for cars.
explanation: True. It covers cars, vans and small trucks.

prompt: Class ___ is the step after G1.
explanation: Class G2 follows G1.

prompt: Why is it called graduated?
explanation: Rules ease as you move up each step.

prompt: A new driver gets full privileges at once.
explanation: False. Privileges are earned step by step.

prompt: A G1 driver must have an accompanying driver.
explanation: True. G1 drivers may not drive alone.

prompt: Who must sit beside a G1 driver?
explanation: G1 needs an accompanying driver (4+ years), zero blood alcohol, and time and highway limits: no midnight-to-5 a.m., no 400-series.

prompt: A G1 driver's blood alcohol must be ___.
explanation: G1 drivers must have zero blood alcohol.

prompt: G1 drivers may drive alone.
explanation: False. An accompanying driver must sit in the front seat.

prompt: Which hours are off-limits for G1?
explanation: G1 drivers must not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.

prompt: The accompanying driver needs ___ years of experience.
explanation: The accompanying driver needs at least four years of experience.

prompt: G1 drivers may use any highway.
explanation: False. Fast 400-series highways (posted over 80 km/h) are off-limits.

prompt: Where does the accompanying driver sit?
explanation: The accompanying driver sits in the front passenger seat.

prompt: G2 drivers 19 and under have passenger limits.
explanation: True. They apply between midnight and 5 a.m.

prompt: What is the G2 blood alcohol limit?
explanation: G2 drivers must also have zero blood alcohol. Drivers 19 and under are limited to one passenger aged 19 or under at first.

prompt: G2 drivers may drink and drive a little.
explanation: False. G2 drivers must have zero blood alcohol.

prompt: G2 drivers must have ___ blood alcohol.
explanation: The limit is zero.

prompt: Passenger limits apply between midnight and ___.
explanation: They apply from midnight to 5 a.m.

prompt: Drivers 21 and under must have zero blood alcohol.
explanation: True. This applies regardless of licence class.

prompt: G1 usually lasts twelve months.
explanation: True. An approved course can shorten it.

prompt: How long is G1 with an approved course?
explanation: G1 lasts twelve months, or eight months after an approved beginner driver education course of at least 40 hours.

prompt: G1 normally lasts ___ months.
explanation: G1 normally lasts twelve months.

prompt: With an approved course, G1 can be ___ months.
explanation: An approved course reduces it to eight months.

prompt: Beginner driver education is at least 40 hours.
explanation: True. The course must be at least 40 hours.

prompt: What shortens G1 by four months?
explanation: Completing approved beginner driver education does.

prompt: A course makes G1 last longer.
explanation: False. It shortens G1 from twelve to eight months.

prompt: Beginner driver ___ shortens G1.
explanation: Beginner driver education is the approved course.

prompt: You must pass a vision test to get licensed.
explanation: True. It is one of the first steps.

prompt: Which test checks your eyesight?
explanation: Pass a vision test, show original identity documents (proof of name and birth date), and later pass two road tests.

prompt: Identity documents must be originals.
explanation: True. Original, valid proof of name and birth date is required.

prompt: Applicants must pass a ___ test.
explanation: A vision test is required.

prompt: How many road tests are there?
explanation: There are two road tests: one to leave G1 and one to leave G2.

prompt: Identity documents can be photocopies.
explanation: False. You must show original documents.

prompt: Which proves your name and birth date?
explanation: A valid passport is an acceptable original document.

prompt: You take ___ road tests in total.
explanation: One at the end of G1 and one at the end of G2.

prompt: New residents get sixty days to use their old licence.
explanation: True. Some licences can also be exchanged.

prompt: How long can new residents use an old licence?
explanation: New residents get a sixty-day grace period to use their licence. Licence exchange is possible for some provinces and countries.

prompt: Some foreign licences can be exchanged for an Ontario one.
explanation: True. Licences from some countries and provinces can be exchanged.

prompt: New residents have ___ days.
explanation: The grace period is sixty days.

prompt: What can some residents do with licences?
explanation: They can exchange it for an Ontario licence.

prompt: Licence exchange means retaking all tests.
explanation: False. Some licences can be exchanged without full testing.

prompt: The test has signs and rules sections.
explanation: True. Each section is marked separately.

prompt: How many questions are on the G1 test?
explanation: The G1 knowledge test has 40 questions: 20 on road signs, 20 on rules of the road. Pass mark: 16 correct per section.

prompt: The test has ___ questions.
explanation: There are 40 questions.

prompt: You need ___ correct in each section.
explanation: The pass mark is 16 correct in each section.

prompt: The test has two sections.
explanation: True. One is road signs and one is rules of the road.

prompt: How many signs questions are there?
explanation: There are 20 questions on road signs.

prompt: You pass with 16 correct overall.
explanation: False. You need 16 correct in each section.

prompt: What is the pass mark per section?
explanation: You need 16 correct in the signs section and 16 in the rules section.

prompt: You must wait ten days between failed tests.
explanation: True. This applies before you retry.

prompt: How long must you wait after a failed test?
explanation: The waiting period after a failed test is at least 10 days before you can retake it.

prompt: Wait at least ___ days to retry.
explanation: The minimum wait is ten days.

prompt: You can retake a failed test the next day.
explanation: False. You must wait at least ten days.

prompt: The waiting period applies between tests.
explanation: True. You must wait at least 10 days between tests.

prompt: G1 comes first, then G2, then full G.
explanation: True. Each step has its own rules.

prompt: How many road tests are needed in total?
explanation: Two road tests: one to leave G1 and one to leave G2.

prompt: Match each item to its meaning.
options: G1↔Learner stage|G2↔Second stage|Class G↔Full licence|BDE↔Course shortens G1
explanation: Each item is part of the licensing steps.

prompt: Drivers 21 and under need blood alcohol ___.
explanation: Zero blood alcohol is required.

prompt: The knowledge test needs 16 correct per section.
explanation: True. There are two sections of 20 questions.

prompt: Which test is for eyesight?
explanation: The vision test checks your eyesight.

prompt: Eight months applies after an approved course.
explanation: True. Approved beginner driver education shortens G1 to eight months.

prompt: Wait ___ days after a failed test.
explanation: You must wait at least ten days.

prompt: Match each term, round 1.
options: Graduated licensing↔Three-step licence|Beginner driver education↔40-hour course
explanation: Each term goes with its short meaning.

prompt: Sign shapes warn you before you read.
explanation: True. Each shape has its own meaning.

prompt: What shape is a stop sign?
explanation: A stop sign is an octagon, yield is a triangle, warning signs are diamonds and regulatory signs are rectangles.

prompt: A yield sign is a triangle.
explanation: True. A yield sign is a downward-pointing triangle.

prompt: What shape are most warning signs?
explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with a yellow background.

prompt: Regulatory signs are usually ___ in shape.
explanation: Regulatory signs, which give rules, are usually rectangular.

prompt: A stop sign is a triangle.
explanation: False. A stop sign is an octagon.

prompt: Which sign is a triangle?
explanation: A yield sign is a triangle.

prompt: Diamond signs warn you about hazards.
explanation: True. Yellow diamonds warn of hazards ahead.

prompt: What shape is this sign?
explanation: A speed limit sign is rectangular.

prompt: A yield sign is shaped like a ___.
explanation: A yield sign is a triangle.

prompt: Sign colours carry meaning too.
explanation: True. Colour tells you the sign type.

prompt: What colour are warning signs?
explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols; orange means temporary; red and white mark regulatory signs.

prompt: What colour are construction signs?
explanation: Orange signs warn of temporary conditions such as roadwork.

prompt: Orange signs mean temporary conditions.
explanation: True. Orange is used for construction and other temporary hazards.

prompt: What colour is a stop sign?
explanation: A stop sign is red with white letters.

prompt: Guide signs are usually ___.
explanation: Information and direction signs are typically green with white letters.

prompt: Yellow signs warn you about hazards.
explanation: True. Yellow diamonds warn of hazards ahead.

prompt: What colour is this sign?
explanation: Orange means construction or another temporary condition.

prompt: A stop sign means a complete stop.
explanation: True. Stop behind the line.

prompt: What must you do at this sign?
explanation: Stop sign: stop completely at the line, then go when safe. Yield sign: slow down or stop and give way.

prompt: At a yield sign you may never stop.
explanation: False. Slow down or stop if needed, then go when the way is clear.

prompt: What does this sign mean?
explanation: Yield means slow down or stop and let others go first.

prompt: At a yield sign, slow down or ___.
explanation: At a yield sign you slow down or stop until the way is clear.

prompt: A rolling stop is allowed at a stop sign.
explanation: False. You must make a complete stop.

prompt: Speed limit signs show the maximum speed.
explanation: True. Speeds are in kilometres an hour.

prompt: What does this sign tell you?
explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum speed in km/h. A no parking sign and a no stopping sign limit where you stop.

prompt: Speed limits are in miles per hour.
explanation: False. Ontario signs use kilometres per hour.

prompt: The maximum speed here is ___ km/h.
explanation: This sign shows a maximum of 80 km/h.

prompt: What does this sign mean?
explanation: No parking means you may not park there.

prompt: A no parking sign means you may park briefly.
explanation: False. Do not park where this sign applies.

prompt: Which sign forbids stopping?
explanation: A no stopping sign means you may not stop there at all.

prompt: This sign allows stopping briefly.
explanation: False. No stopping means you may not stop there.

prompt: A red circle with a bar means do not enter.
explanation: True. Never drive in.

prompt: What does this sign mean?
explanation: Do not enter. Never drive past it, because you would be going the wrong way.

prompt: You may enter past this sign.
explanation: False. Entering would put you against traffic.

prompt: What kind of street is this?
explanation: Traffic goes only in the direction of the arrow.

prompt: An arrow sign shows ___ traffic direction.
explanation: A one-way sign shows the only allowed direction.

prompt: What does this sign warn you about?
explanation: You are going the wrong way. Stop and turn around safely.

prompt: You may back down a one-way street.
explanation: False. Travel only in the signed direction.

prompt: Which sign shows you entering wrongly?
explanation: A wrong way sign means you have entered against traffic.

prompt: Turn signs forbid certain moves.
explanation: True. Obey them every time.

prompt: Which turn does this ban?
explanation: A red circle with a slash bans the turn shown, such as no left turn or no U-turn. Keep right signs say stay right.

prompt: This sign allows left turns.
explanation: False. The slash means that turn is forbidden.

prompt: What does this sign forbid?
explanation: The slashed arrow shows a right turn is banned.

prompt: Which move does this ban?
explanation: You may not make a U-turn here.

prompt: This sign forbids ___.
explanation: A slashed U-shaped arrow forbids U-turns.

prompt: What must you do at this sign?
explanation: Keep to the right of the barrier or island.

prompt: This sign says to pass on the left side.
explanation: False. Keep right of the obstruction.

prompt: Signs you know protect you.
explanation: True. Review the basics.

prompt: Which step needs an accompanying driver?
explanation: G1 drivers must have an accompanying driver.

prompt: Which sign has an octagon shape?
explanation: Only the stop sign is an octagon.

prompt: What does this sign mean?
explanation: A red circle with a white bar means do not enter.

prompt: Yellow diamonds are warning signs.
explanation: True. They warn of hazards ahead.

prompt: Speed limit signs show the ___ speed.
explanation: They show the maximum allowed speed.

prompt: Which sign bans stopping there?
explanation: A no stopping sign means you may not stop there.

prompt: Wait ten days after a failed test.
explanation: True. You must wait at least ten days before retaking.

prompt: A curve sign means slow down for the bend.
explanation: True. Check the advisory speed.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: A curve warning: slow down before the bend. Signs also show a steep hill or a winding road.

prompt: What does 18% show?
explanation: A steep hill ahead. The percentage shows how steep the grade is.

prompt: This sign means a straight road.
explanation: False. It warns of a winding road.

prompt: This sign warns of a ___ road.
explanation: A winding road has several curves in a row.

prompt: Which way does the road bend?
explanation: The road bends sharply to the right ahead.

prompt: Slow down before entering a curve.
explanation: True. Hard braking inside a curve can make you lose control.

prompt: Which way does the curve warning turn?
explanation: The road turns left ahead at about ninety degrees.

prompt: A cross-shaped sign warns of an intersection.
explanation: True. Watch for crossing traffic.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: An intersection ahead: watch for traffic from both sides. A traffic signal ahead sign warns of lights.

prompt: A T-shaped sign means your road ends.
explanation: True. It warns of a T-intersection ahead.

prompt: What is ahead?
explanation: Traffic lights are ahead. Watch for them and be ready to stop.

prompt: This sign warns a stop is ___.
explanation: A stop sign ahead gives you time to slow down.

prompt: This sign means a yield sign is ahead.
explanation: True. Be ready to slow down or stop.

prompt: Warning signs show how the road changes.
explanation: True. Read them early.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: One lane ends ahead; move over early. Other signs show where a divided road begins or ends.

prompt: This sign means a new lane starts.
explanation: False. A lane ends ahead.

prompt: What does this sign show?
explanation: A divider separates opposite traffic ahead. Keep to your side.

prompt: Here the road ___ into two separate roadways.
explanation: A median begins, separating opposite directions of traffic.

prompt: What changes ahead?
explanation: The median ends. Expect two-way traffic on one roadway.

prompt: After this sign, oncoming traffic shares your road.
explanation: True. The divider ends, so be alert for oncoming vehicles.

prompt: Which sign shows pavement narrowing?
explanation: A road narrows sign warns the pavement gets narrower.

prompt: Watch for children near schools and parks.
explanation: True. They may run into the road.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: A pedestrian crossing: slow down and be ready to stop. Also watch for a school zone or playground.

prompt: What does this sign mean?
explanation: A school zone. Watch for children and obey the lower speed.

prompt: A school zone sign is fluorescent yellow-green.
explanation: True. School signs are fluorescent yellow-green.

prompt: This sign warns of a ___.
explanation: Children may run into the road near a playground.

prompt: What is the hazard here?
explanation: Slow down; children may run out suddenly.

prompt: You may ignore school signs on weekends.
explanation: False. Always watch for children near schools.

prompt: What does this sign show?
explanation: At a pedestrian crossover, stop and yield to pedestrians.

prompt: Trains cannot stop quickly.
explanation: True. They need a very long distance.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: Advance warning: a railway crossing is ahead. The crossing has an X-shaped sign; slow down and look both ways.

prompt: Trains can stop quickly.
explanation: False. A train needs a very long distance to stop.

prompt: What shape marks the crossing itself?
explanation: The crossing sign is X-shaped, white with a red outline.

prompt: Stop at least ___ metres from the nearest rail.
explanation: Stop at least 5 metres from the nearest rail or gate.

prompt: Which sign is the advance warning?
explanation: The yellow diamond warns you before the crossing.

prompt: You may go around lowered gates at the crossing.
explanation: False. Never go around or under gates.

prompt: You may race a train at the crossing.
explanation: False. Never race a train.

prompt: Road surface signs warn of changes.
explanation: True. Adjust speed early.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: A slippery when wet sign: slow down. Other signs warn of a bump or a narrow bridge.

prompt: This sign warns of a bump ahead.
explanation: True. Slow down before the bump.

prompt: What is ahead?
explanation: A raised hump in the road ahead.

prompt: This sign warns of a ___ bridge.
explanation: The bridge is narrower than the road.

prompt: What does this sign mean?
explanation: The bridge ahead is narrow. Slow down and stay in your lane.

prompt: Slippery signs apply only in winter.
explanation: False. Wet roads are slippery in any season.

prompt: What changes ahead?
explanation: The paved surface ends. Slow down for gravel or dirt.

prompt: Warning signs tell you what is ahead.
explanation: True. Review them once more.

prompt: What colour is a warning sign?
explanation: Warning signs are yellow diamonds with black symbols.

prompt: What is the hazard?
explanation: The road may be slippery. Slow down.

prompt: This sign marks a school zone.
explanation: True. Watch for children.

prompt: What lies ahead?
explanation: A railway crossing is ahead.

prompt: An octagon always means ___.
explanation: An octagon means stop.

prompt: Which road is shown?
explanation: Several curves in a row ahead.

prompt: Yield signs are triangles.
explanation: True. Slow down or stop if needed.

prompt: Orange signs warn of temporary hazards.
explanation: True. Work zones change often.

prompt: What does this sign warn of?
explanation: Orange signs mean construction: slow down for workers ahead. A flagger ahead may stop you.

prompt: Orange signs apply only while work continues.
explanation: True. They mark temporary conditions.

prompt: Who may be ahead?
explanation: Workers are on or near the road. Slow down.

prompt: Slow down when workers are ___.
explanation: Workers may be close to your lane.

prompt: What should you do?
explanation: Slow down and prepare to stop; a flagger or temporary signal ahead may stop you.

prompt: This orange sign shows a lower speed.
explanation: True. Obey the construction-zone limit.

prompt: What is changing ahead?
explanation: Be ready to follow a different route.

prompt: Green signs guide you to places.
explanation: True. They give directions.

prompt: What colour are guide signs?
explanation: Green guide signs, such as exit signs and distance signs, have white letters.

prompt: Guide signs give directions.
explanation: True. They name places and exits.

prompt: Exit signs help you ___.
explanation: They show where to leave the highway.

prompt: What do distance signs show?
explanation: They show how far places are in kilometres.

prompt: Guide signs are orange.
explanation: False. Guide signs are green.

prompt: Which sign names the next town?
explanation: Green guide signs name destinations.

prompt: Exit signs are green.
explanation: True. Exit and direction signs are green with white letters.

prompt: Traffic lights control who goes.
explanation: True. Obey them.

prompt: What does a red light mean?
explanation: Red: stop (right turn allowed after stopping unless signed). Yellow: prepare to stop. Green: go carefully.

prompt: What does a green light mean?
explanation: Proceed with care, yielding to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.

prompt: Yellow means speed up.
explanation: False. Yellow means red is coming; stop if you can do so safely.

prompt: Yellow means the light is about to turn ___.
explanation: Stop if you can safely; otherwise proceed with caution.

prompt: What must you do at this light?
explanation: Red means stop completely.

prompt: Which light means get ready to stop?
explanation: Yellow means red is about to appear.

prompt: After stopping at red, a right turn may be allowed.
explanation: True. Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right after stopping and yielding.

prompt: Flashing lights need extra care.
explanation: True. Their meanings differ from steady lights.

prompt: What does a flashing red light mean?
explanation: Flashing red: stop, then go when safe. Flashing yellow: caution. A green arrow lets you turn.

prompt: Flashing yellow means proceed with caution.
explanation: True. Slow down and watch for hazards.

prompt: What does this light mean?
explanation: Slow down and proceed with caution.

prompt: What does a green arrow mean?
explanation: You may turn in the arrow's direction; the signal protects the turn.

prompt: A flashing green allows turning left.
explanation: True. It is an advance green, so you may turn or go straight.

prompt: Unlike a green arrow, yellow means ___ turning.
explanation: A yellow arrow means do not start your left turn; red is coming.

prompt: If the lights are out, treat it as ___.
explanation: A signal that is out works like an all-way stop.

prompt: Pedestrian signals protect walkers.
explanation: True. Watch for them.

prompt: What does this signal mean?
explanation: A walking person means cross. An orange hand means do not start crossing.

prompt: What does an orange hand mean?
explanation: Do not start crossing.

prompt: A steady hand means finish crossing quickly.
explanation: True. If already crossing, finish quickly; do not start.

prompt: A flashing hand means do not ___ crossing.
explanation: A flashing orange hand means do not start crossing.

prompt: Pedestrians may cross on a left-turn arrow.
explanation: False. They may not cross on a flashing green or left-turn arrow.

prompt: What does a white walking person mean?
explanation: It means it is safe for pedestrians to begin crossing.

prompt: Drivers must yield to people still crossing.
explanation: True. Wait for them to clear the intersection.

prompt: Line colours show traffic direction.
explanation: True. Yellow separates opposing traffic.

prompt: What do yellow lines separate?
explanation: Yellow lines separate opposite directions; white lines separate the same direction. A bike lane line is solid white.

prompt: What do white lines separate?
explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same way.

prompt: Yellow lines separate same-direction lanes.
explanation: False. They separate opposite directions.

prompt: White lines separate ___ traffic.
explanation: White lane lines separate traffic travelling the same way.

prompt: A solid white line marks ___.
explanation: A solid white line marks a bike lane.

prompt: Bike lanes are marked by a solid white line.
explanation: True. Do not drive in them.

prompt: Which line colour is on your left?
explanation: On a two-way road the centre line is yellow.

prompt: Line patterns tell you whether to pass.
explanation: True. Broken lines allow passing.

prompt: A solid yellow line on your side means ___.
explanation: Solid line on your side: don't pass. Broken line: pass if clear. Continuity lines have wider, closer dashes.

prompt: A broken yellow line allows safe passing.
explanation: True. Pass only when it is clear.

prompt: What does this line mean?
explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass when it is clear.

prompt: Pass only when the way is ___.
explanation: Check for oncoming traffic before passing.

prompt: Which line means don't pass?
explanation: A solid yellow line on your side bans passing.

prompt: Continuity lines have wider, closer dashes.
explanation: True. They mark a lane that ends or continues.

prompt: Continuity line on your left means ___.
explanation: A continuity line on the left means your lane is ending.

prompt: A stop line shows where to stop.
explanation: True. Stop before it.

prompt: What is a stop line?
explanation: A stop line is a single white line. A crosswalk has two white lines; a pedestrian crossover adds X marks.

prompt: Stop beyond the stop line.
explanation: False. Stop before the line, not over it.

prompt: A crosswalk is two parallel ___ lines.
explanation: Two parallel white lines mark a crosswalk.

prompt: What does this marking show?
explanation: Two parallel white lines mark a crosswalk.

prompt: What marks a pedestrian crossover?
explanation: Double white lines with an X in each approaching lane mark a crossover.

prompt: You must yield at a pedestrian crossover.
explanation: True. Stop and let pedestrians cross.

prompt: Which is the stop line?
explanation: A single solid white line across your lane.

prompt: Arrows on the road tell you where to go.
explanation: True. They show the lane direction.

prompt: What does a white lane arrow show?
explanation: Move only in the arrow's direction. Solid lines around objects guide you away from them.

prompt: A straight arrow allows left turns.
explanation: False. A straight arrow means go straight ahead.

prompt: Follow the arrow in your ___.
explanation: Arrows show which way traffic in that lane may go.

prompt: Solid lines around objects guide you ___.
explanation: They guide you away from the hazard.

prompt: Yellow and black markings may be on objects.
explanation: True. They warn you of the hazard.

prompt: Lights and lines work together.
explanation: True. Review the basics.

prompt: Red light means?
explanation: Come to a complete stop.

prompt: A flashing red light means?
explanation: Treat it like a stop sign.

prompt: A walking person means pedestrians may cross.
explanation: True. A white walking person means walk.

prompt: What does a solid yellow line mean?
explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means do not pass.

prompt: A stop line is a ___ line.
explanation: It is a white line.

prompt: A green arrow means?
explanation: You may turn in the arrow's direction.

prompt: Yellow lines separate opposite directions.
explanation: True. White lines separate the same direction.

prompt: Everyone in the car must wear a seatbelt.
explanation: True. The driver is responsible for checking.

prompt: Who must wear a seatbelt?
explanation: Check your vehicle and adjust mirrors. Everyone must buckle up; airbags do not replace seatbelts, and not buckling brings a fine.

prompt: Everyone in the car must wear a ___.
explanation: A seatbelt is required for everyone in the car.

prompt: Airbags replace seatbelts.
explanation: False. Airbags do not replace seatbelts.

prompt: What should you adjust before driving?
explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see around the vehicle.

prompt: Not wearing a seatbelt can bring a fine.
explanation: True. Buckling up is the law.

prompt: Check your ___ before driving.
explanation: Check that your vehicle is safe to drive.

prompt: Do airbags replace seatbelts?
explanation: No. Seatbelts are still required.

prompt: Hold the steering wheel at nine and three.
explanation: True. Steer smoothly and precisely.

prompt: Hold the wheel at ___ and three o'clock.
explanation: Hand position: nine and three o'clock. Smooth steering is precise. Set the parking brake whenever you park.

prompt: Steering should be smooth and precise.
explanation: True. Jerky steering reduces control.

prompt: Set the ___ brake when you park.
explanation: Always set the parking brake when you park.

prompt: Which hand position is correct?
explanation: The handbook recommends nine and three o'clock.

prompt: Steering with one hand is best.
explanation: False. Use both hands at nine and three.

prompt: When should you set the parking brake?
explanation: Set it whenever you park.

prompt: Steer ___ and precisely.
explanation: Steering should be smooth and precise.

prompt: Posted speed limits always apply.
explanation: True. Defaults apply only when no limit is posted.

prompt: What is the default limit in cities?
explanation: Obey the posted speed limit. The default limit in built-up areas is 50 km/h; elsewhere it is 80 km/h.

prompt: The default limit elsewhere is ___ km/h.
explanation: Outside cities, towns and villages the default is 80 km/h.

prompt: Posted limits apply over defaults.
explanation: True. A posted sign overrides the default.

prompt: What is the default limit in towns?
explanation: Towns default to 50 km/h.

prompt: The default limit in cities is 80 km/h.
explanation: False. It is 50 km/h in cities, towns and villages.

prompt: Villages default to ___ km/h.
explanation: Villages default to 50 km/h.

prompt: Which sign overrides defaults?
explanation: A posted speed limit sign does.

prompt: Leave at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead.
explanation: True. This is the minimum gap.

prompt: What is the minimum following gap?
explanation: Following distance is the gap behind the vehicle ahead. Keep at least two seconds (the two-second rule), more in bad weather or behind trucks.

prompt: Keep a ___-second gap.
explanation: The minimum is two seconds.

prompt: Two seconds suits bad weather.
explanation: False. Bad weather needs more space.

prompt: When do you need more space?
explanation: Leave extra space in bad weather or behind trucks.

prompt: The two-second rule gives a minimum gap.
explanation: True. It is a minimum, for good conditions.

prompt: Your car keeps moving while you react.
explanation: True. That adds to your stopping distance.

prompt: ___ time is how long you take to respond.
